PC: Obtains history of present illness, past medical history, past surgical history, medication history, history of allergies, family history and past obstetric/gynecologic history
Assesses vital signs
Performs physical examination that must include (at a minimum) evaluation of chest, lungs, abdomen, extremities and pelvis
Orders the following laboratory tests: complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, uric acid, urine protein/creatinine ratio
Appropriately assesses fetal heart rate tracing and contraction pattern
Optional: Performs transabdominal sonogram, requests findings verbally
Asks for repeat blood pressure 15 minutes after initial one was obtained
Asks for repeat blood pressure in 10 or 20 minutes depending on antihypertensive administered
Protects airway
Obtains pulse oximetry
Places patient in left lateral decubitus
Ensures bedrails are up and pads bedrails
Establishes suction at bedside
Continues magnesium infusion
Intravenous (IV) access/labs
Supplement oxygen (100% non-rebreather)
Bag-mask ventilation on the unit
Continuous fetal monitoring (if appropriate)
Load 4-6 grams 10% magnesium sulfate in 100 ml solution IV over 20 minutes
Magnesium sulfate on infusion pump
Magnesium sulfate 10 grams of 50% solution intramuscular (5 grams in each buttock) if no IV access
Magnesium sulfate maintenance 1-2 grams/hour continuous infusion

Antihypertensive treatment regimens

• Administer labetalol 20 milligrams (mg) IV:

Recheck blood pressure 10 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer labetalol 40 mg IV

Recheck blood pressure 10 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer labetalol 80 mg IV

Recheck blood pressure 10 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer hydralazine 10 mg IV

Recheck blood pressure 20 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, consult with maternal fetal medicine specialist or

intensive care specialist

• Administer hydralazine 5 mg IV or 10 mg IV

Recheck blood pressure 20 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer hydralazine 10 mg IV

Recheck blood pressure 20 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer labetalol 20 mg IV

Recheck blood pressure 10 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer labetalol 40 mg IV and consult

with maternal fetal medicine specialist or intensive care specialist

• Administer nifedipine 10 mg orally

Recheck blood pressure 20 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer nifedipine 20 mg orally

Recheck blood pressure 20 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer nifedipine 20 mg orally

Recheck blood pressure 20 minutes later

If blood pressure remains elevated, administer labetalol 20 mg IV and consult with

maternal fetal medicine specialist or intensive care specialist

Anticonvulsant medications

(for recurrent seizures or when magnesium sulfate is contraindicated):

• Lorazepam (2-4 mg IV x 1, may repeat x 1 after 10-15 minutes)

• Diazepam (5-10 mg IV every 5-10 minutes to maximum dose 30 mg)

• Phenytoin (15-20 mg/kg IV x 1, may repeat 10 mg/kg IV after 20 minutes if no response); avoid with hypotension, may cause cardiac

arrhythmias

• Levetiracetam (500 mg IV or orally, may repeat in 12 hours); dose adjustment needed if renal impairment
SBP: Call for assistance (Hospital should identify a Rapid Response Team) to location of the event

Check in:

Obstetric Attendings/ Fellows/Residents

Three registered nurses

Anesthesia

Neonatology (if indicated)
Appoint a primary RN and secondary personnel
ICS: Explains clinical findings and plan to patient and addresses patient concerns
Checks back with fellow learners regarding medication administration
